turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning from device physics and training patterns

**What the training data says about high-efficiency p-i-n MAPbI3 recipes:**

1. **PTAA as HTL + Cu back contact** is the strongest recurring motif: C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu gives 18.4–19.1 (spin, slot-die, doctor blading), PCBM-60|C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu = 18.85, PTAA|PFN / Cu|Ag = 18.8. PTAA's deep HOMO (~ -5.2 eV) aligns well with MAPbI3 valence band, is hydrophobic (good perovskite wetting/crystallization templates) and low-doped → low interface recombination; Cu is cheap, low-diffusivity, and doesn't form insulating AgI.

2. **Passivated fullerene stacks on P3CT-Na**: ITCPTC-Th | C60 | BCP / P3CT-Na = 18.49; P3CT-Na|PASP = 18.98. Perylene-diimide-type acceptors with a C60|BCP capping give excellent electron selectivity and defect passivation.

3. **PMMA-passivated PTAA**: PCBM-60|Bphen / PTAA|PMMA / Al = 19.48 — ultrathin PMMA passivates the buried interface.

4. **Plasmonic/modified NiO-c**: Au-np|NiO-c = 20.0, NiO-c|SDBS = 19.04, [BMIM]BF4-modified = 21.33 — interface-engineered NiO-c is among the best HTLs.

**Mapping to candidates:**

- **c044** (PCBM-60|BCP / PTAA / Cu, spin-coating): near-exact analog of 18.6–18.85 training rows. Excellent selectivity, no AgI corrosion.
- **c088** (Willow glass|ITO, C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu, doctor blading): C60|BCP/none/Cu blading = 18.4, PTAA/Cu slot-die = 19.1 → same physics, high expected PCE.
- **c030** (IDTT2FPDI|PCBM-60|Bphen / PTAA|PMMA / Al): direct analog of the 19.48 row with an added NFA interlayer that passivates traps.
- **c097** (ITCPTC-Se|C60|BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag): Se analog of the 18.49 Th device; Se substitution typically improves electron mobility slightly.
- **c038** (PCBM-60|PEI / Au-np|NiO-c / Ag): the Au-np|NiO-c HTL gave 20.0 in training; plasmonic enhancement + good NiO band alignment; PEI dipole lowers electron-extraction barrier (some risk from PEI thickness, so ranked last of five).

Runner-ups considered: c034 (PTAA/Al, ~18), c041 (NiMgLiO-c ~18), c039 (TiO2-c capped/NiO-c = 17.4), c085, c079 — all slightly below the chosen set.

**Final: c044, c088, c030, c097, c038**
